pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

This PR contains several changes to allow users to fetch newly created dashboards and folders. 

The changes are:
* on client side: remove the use of authLib cache when running authZ service in-proc
* on server side: add a denial cache to return quickly when we know that a user does not have permission on a specific resource
* on server side: if permission denial cache is not hit, and the requested resource is not found in cached permissions, requery permissions from the DB

**Why do we need this feature?**

Otherwise dash/folder creator can't access the dashboard/folder that they've just created.

**Who is this feature for?**

Grafana users

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/identity-access-team/issues/1316
pr.title: AuthZService: improve authz caching

raw_findings.body: The denial-cache lookup returns early with Allowed:false before the newly added getIdentityPermissions requery-from-DB path runs, so the user is wrongly denied for up to shortCacheTTL even though the DB now grants access — directly undermining the PR goal of letting creators access freshly granted resources.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authorization returns a stale deny that contradicts current DB state.
raw_findings.impact: The denial-cache lookup returns early with Allowed:false before the newly added getIdentityPermissions requery-from-DB path runs, so the user is wrongly denied for up to shortCacheTTL even though the DB now grants access — directly undermining the PR goal of letting creators access freshly granted resources.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new permDenialCache is consulted before the requery logic and has no invalidation hook tied to permission changes.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Invalidate (Delete) the matching permDenialCache entries when permissions change / when getIdentityPermissions returns a grant, or drop the denial cache short-circuit in favor of the requery path when a grant is possible; at minimum document and bound the staleness window explicitly.
raw_findings.title: Denial cache short-circuits requery and is never invalidated on permission grant
raw_findings.trigger: A user does a Check on a (name,parent) resource they cannot yet access; the denial is cached (shortCacheTTL, 30s). The permission is then granted in the DB (e.g. a folder/dashboard permission is added) within that TTL, and the same subject re-checks the same name+parent.

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the denial-cache population logic (wrong key, missing Set, wrong condition) would not be caught, since no test asserts that a DB-denied Check populates permDenialCache and that a subsequent identical Check is served from that cache.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test suite passes despite a broken denial-cache population.
raw_findings.impact: Regressions in the denial-cache population logic (wrong key, missing Set, wrong condition) would not be caught, since no test asserts that a DB-denied Check populates permDenialCache and that a subsequent identical Check is served from that cache.
raw_findings.root_cause: New denial-cache Set branch added without accompanying coverage of the write path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that performs a Check which the store denies, then asserts permDenialCache now contains userPermDenialCacheKey(...) and that a following identical Check returns Allowed:false without hitting the store.
raw_findings.title: Denial-cache write path is not exercised by any test
raw_findings.trigger: A Check whose DB result is not allowed executes this branch; TestService_CacheCheck only pre-populates permDenialCache manually and never validates that a real DB denial writes an entry.

finding.title: Denial cache short-circuits requery and is never invalidated on permission grant
finding.trigger: A user does a Check on a (name,parent) resource they cannot yet access; the denial is cached (shortCacheTTL, 30s). The permission is then granted in the DB (e.g. a folder/dashboard permission is added) within that TTL, and the same subject re-checks the same name+parent.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch shows that after the denial cache check (line 117-121), the code proceeds to getCachedIdentityPermissions (line 123) and if that returns a grant (allowed=true at line 131), it returns allowed. If the permission cache misses, it calls getIdentityPermissions from DB (line 139) and checks again. The denial cache only short-circuits when the exact (namespace, user, action, name, parent) tuple was previously denied. If permissions change in DB, the next getIdentityPermissions call would return the new grant. The claim that denial cache prevents requery is incorrect - the denial cache is checked first, but if it hits, it means that specific resource was denied before. The requery path (getIdentityPermissions) is for when permission cache misses, not for invalidating denial cache. The design appears intentional: cache denials for specific resources to avoid repeated DB lookups for the same denied resource within TTL.

finding.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage suggestion, not a bug. The candidate claims the denial-cache write path at line 154 lacks test coverage. While this may be true, test gaps are stylistic/quality concerns rather than defects introduced by the patch. The patch itself is functional - the Set call at line 154 is correctly placed after checkPermission returns !allowed. The absence of a specific test exercising this path does not constitute a bug in the implementation.
